newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rates not seen rising soon - Sakakibara quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan rates not seen rising soon - Sakakibara quoted.

text.p: Japan interest rates are unlikely to rise anytime soon, given current economic conditions, senior Finance Mininstry official Eisuke Sakakibara was quoted as telling a financial seminar on Thursday.
The comments were relayed to reporters by a participant in the seminar.
"It is unlikely that Japan's interest rates will be raised soon, given that the economic data for the April-June period will not be good," the participant quoted Sakakibara as saying.
Japan may have to wait until later this year before a decision is made on interest rates, Sakakibara was quoted as saying.
Another participant at the seminar quoted Sakakibara as saying that Japan's trade surplus was unlikely to be a major issue at the Group of Seven (G7) nations' meeting in Denver from June 20-22.
